title: The Great Acceleration and the proposed (rejected) Anthropocene epoch
summary: The Great Acceleration is the synchronous speed-up, from the 1950s on, of 24 indicators of human activity and Earth-system change. In 2023 the Anthropocene Working Group proposed that a new epoch began between 1950 and 1954, marked by plutonium from nuclear testing in the sediment of Crawford Lake, near Toronto. In a statement of 26 March 2024, the IUGS and the International Commission on Stratigraphy confirmed that the Subcommission on Quaternary Stratigraphy had voted to reject the proposal.

uncertainty.note: Future Earth says the synchronous acceleration runs "from the 1950s to the present day" (ongoing; the end year here is a placeholder for now). The Working Group proposal names 1950 to 1954 for the epoch start.

beats.caption: Twenty-four indicators, 12 socio-economic and 12 Earth-system, accelerate together from the 1950s.
Geologists point to a plutonium layer from nuclear testing in the sediment of Crawford Lake in Ontario as a marker.
The Anthropocene Working Group proposes naming the start of a new epoch between 1950 and 1954.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the formal status. I did not open any page on whether the epoch was ratified, so the summary says only that a proposal was made in 2023; check before upgrading. Crawford Lake is a sourced type site (Al Jazeera, EarthSky) but the record is planet-wide, so uncertainty is 5000 km. The "24 indicators" and "from the 1950s" claims are from Future Earth. End year 2025 is a placeholder for an ongoing process.
